Properties

All configurable properties exposed on the Button component.

Attribute Type Default Description
style enum filled Visual style. One of filled · outlined · clear · filled-reversed · outlined-reversed · clear-reversed · super-cta-fill · super-cta-overlay. Reversed variants are pinned to light-mode primitives — they don't re-theme in dark mode.
size enum large One of large · medium · small. Small uses 16px icons; medium and large use 24px icons.
icon enum none One of none · leading · trailing · icon-only. Super CTA always uses the trailing badge — this property does not apply to that style.
label string — Button label text. Required unless icon=icon-only. Icon-only buttons must have an aria-label.
disabled boolean false Prevents interaction. Use the native disabled attribute — not aria-disabled — so the button is removed from tab order automatically.
fixed-width boolean false When true, the button fills its container width. Useful in form layouts and mobile contexts.

Accessibility

Built on the native <button> element — ARIA roles and keyboard behaviour are handled by the browser.

Keyboard interaction

KeyAction
TabMove focus to the next focusable button.
Shift + TabMove focus to the previous focusable button.
Enter / SpaceActivate the focused button.

ARIA & roles

AttributeGuidance
role="button" Implicit on native <button>. Don't apply it manually unless rendering a non-button element.
aria-label Required on icon-only buttons. Describes the action, not the icon (e.g. "Close dialog", not "X icon").
aria-disabled="true" Avoid. Prefer the native disabled attribute — it removes the element from the tab order and suppresses events automatically.
aria-pressed Use only for toggle buttons (on/off state). Not applicable to standard action buttons.
aria-busy Set to true while the button is loading. Pair with a visible spinner and keep the label descriptive (e.g. "Saving…").

Contrast & motion

  • All button text meets WCAG AA minimum contrast (4.5:1) against their respective backgrounds in both light and dark mode.
  • The Super CTA overlay style meets AA contrast only when placed over sufficiently dark photography. Test each usage in context.
  • Hover and pressed transitions respect prefers-reduced-motion — wrap animation properties in a media query if motion sensitivity is a concern for your audience.

Properties

All configurable properties exposed on the Choice Button component.

Property Values Default Description
layout vertical · horizontal vertical Orientation of the button content. Vertical stacks accessory above label; horizontal places them side by side.
media icon · icon-bullet · avatar icon Type of leading accessory. Icon uses a raw SVG icon; icon-bullet uses the Icon Bullet component; avatar uses a circular photo or initials placeholder.
state default · hover · pressed · focused · selected · disabled default Interactive state of the button. Selected is communicated via aria-pressed="true" and a distinct filled background.
style standard · reversed standard Surface context. Reversed uses inverse tokens pinned to light-mode primitives — for dark backgrounds and overlays. Does not re-theme in dark mode.

Accessibility

Choice buttons use native <button> elements with aria-pressed to communicate selection state to assistive technology.

InteractionBehaviour
role="button" Implicit on native <button>. Communicates interactive nature to assistive technology.
aria-pressed="true/false" Communicates selected/unselected state. Must be updated on every toggle — never omit this attribute on a choice button.
Space / Enter Toggles selection state when the choice button has keyboard focus.
Tab Moves focus to the next choice button (or next focusable element). Each button is individually focusable.
disabled Use the native disabled attribute — not aria-disabled. Removes the button from tab order and prevents all interaction automatically.

Components · Actions

Chip

Compact interactive elements for filtering, sorting, and tagging. Four types — toggle, toggle-strong, dropdown, and dismissible — share a unified pill shape. Chips sit inline with content and are designed to be grouped.

Stable v1.0 Web Mobile Figma ↗

Preview

Interact with the controls to explore chip types and badge variants.

  • Toggle
  • Dropdown
  • Dismissible
  • Toggle-strong
<!-- Toggle chip -->
<button class="chip" aria-pressed="false" type="button">Label</button>

<!-- Toggle chip · selected -->
<button class="chip chip--selected" aria-pressed="true" type="button">Label</button>

<!-- Toggle chip · with badge -->
<button class="chip" aria-pressed="false" type="button">
  Label <span class="chip-badge">4</span>
</button>

<!-- Toggle-strong -->
<button class="chip chip--strong" aria-pressed="false" type="button">Label</button>

<!-- Dropdown chip -->
<button class="chip chip--dropdown" type="button">
  Label
  <svg class="chip-chevron" viewBox="0 0 10 6" fill="none">
    <path d="M1 1L5 5L9 1" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>
  </svg>
</button>

<!-- Dismissible chip -->
<button class="chip chip--dismissible chip--selected" aria-pressed="true" type="button">
  Label
  <svg class="chip-dismiss" viewBox="0 0 14 14" fill="none" aria-label="Remove">
    <path d="M2 2L12 12M12 2L2 12" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round"/>
  </svg>
</button>

<!-- Chip group -->
<div class="chip-group">
  <button class="chip chip--selected" aria-pressed="true"  type="button">All</button>
  <button class="chip" aria-pressed="false" type="button">Design</button>
  <button class="chip" aria-pressed="false" type="button">Motion</button>
</div>

Accessibility

Chips are always rendered as <button> elements — never <div> or <span>. This preserves keyboard focus and native click semantics. Toggle selection state is communicated with aria-pressed.

PatternGuidance
Filter / multi-select Use aria-pressed="true/false" on each <button>. No role needed — button is already interactive.
Sort / single-select Wrap toggle-strong chips in a role="group" container. Use aria-pressed per chip and enforce single-selection in JS.
Dismissible Give the button an accessible name that includes "Remove": aria-label="Remove Design System filter". The × icon should be aria-hidden="true".
Dropdown Use aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-expanded on the chip button. The chevron is decorative (aria-hidden).
Disabled Use the native disabled attribute rather than aria-disabled alone — it removes the chip from the tab order and prevents all interaction.

Properties

ClassValuesDescription
chip — Base chip. 32px tall, full-pill radius, 1.5px border, 14px medium text.
chip--selected — Selected state. 2px ink border, secondary background. Pair with aria-pressed="true".
chip--strong — Toggle-strong variant. 40px tall, 600 font weight. For sort, view, or prominent filter contexts.
chip--dropdown — Indicates the chip opens a menu. Visually identical to toggle — add a .chip-chevron SVG inside to complete the pattern.
chip--dismissible — Chip can be removed. Add a .chip-dismiss SVG inside. JS removes the element on click.
chip--disabled — Disabled visual. Use with the native disabled attribute.
chip-badge — Count pill inside the chip. Inherits selected colour from parent .chip--selected.
chip-group — Flex wrapping row container. Applies 8px gap between chips.

Tags carry no interactive states — they are read-only labels. All visual variety comes from the type, the colour variant, and the optional icon slots.

Variant Label only + Leading icon + Trailing icon

Status

Variant Label only + Leading icon + Trailing icon
Neutral Pending Pending Pending
Success Delivered Delivered Delivered
Warning Delayed Delayed Delayed
Danger Cancelled Cancelled Cancelled

Accessibility

Tags are purely informational and carry no interactive affordances. Their semantics come from placement, colour, and text content — not from role attributes alone.

ConcernImplementation
Element Use <span> for inline tags and <li> inside a <ul> when rendering a group of tags. Never use <button> unless the tag is interactive — use Chips instead.
Icons All icons inside tags are decorative. Always add aria-hidden="true". Never use an icon alone to convey meaning — always pair with a visible text label.
Status colour Colour alone must never be the sole differentiator. The text label (e.g. "Delivered", "Cancelled") communicates the same information as the colour, satisfying WCAG 1.4.1 (Use of Colour).
Contrast All foreground–background combinations meet WCAG AA for small text (4.5:1 minimum). Verify custom themes for compliance before shipping.
Groups When multiple tags appear together as a collection, wrap them in a container with a label — e.g. <ul role="list" aria-label="Applied filters"> — so assistive technology announces the group context.

Properties

Configurable properties shared across both tag families.

PropertyTypeDefaultNotes
type enum — Information: tag--info · tag--emphasis. Status: tag--neutral · tag--success · tag--warning · tag--danger.
label string — Required visible text. Never render an icon-only tag — at minimum a visually-hidden label must be present for screen readers.
leadingIcon boolean false Renders a 16×16 icon before the label. Must include aria-hidden="true". Icon is swappable; defaults to the leading icon slot in the Figma component.
trailingIcon boolean false Renders a 16×16 icon after the label. Must include aria-hidden="true". Icon is swappable; defaults to the trailing icon slot in the Figma component.

Accessibility

Built on the native <a> element — keyboard navigation, focus management, and visited-state tracking are handled by the browser automatically.

PatternGuidance
Element choice Always use a native <a href="…"> for navigation. Never use a <button> or <div> — they break browser history, visited state, and right-click behaviour.
Link text Write labels that make sense out of context. Avoid "click here" or "read more" — screen reader users often browse links as a list.
Decorative icons Mark icon wrappers aria-hidden="true". The visible text label must stand alone as a complete accessible name without the icon.
Disabled Use aria-disabled="true" with pointer-events: none and tabindex="-1". The HTML disabled attribute is not valid on anchor elements.
Focus ring Uses outline rather than box-shadow so it remains visible in Windows High Contrast Mode.

Properties

Attribute Type Default Description
size enum large One of large · medium · small. Controls text size, container height, and icon display size.
icon enum none One of none · leading · trailing. Always use icons from the ůnica icon set at viewBox="0 0 24 24"; size via width/height only.
label string — Required visible text inside .link-text. Must be descriptive enough to make sense out of context.
href string — Required navigation URL on the <a> element. The browser handles visited-state tracking automatically via this attribute.
aria-disabled boolean false Communicates the disabled state to assistive technology. Pair with pointer-events: none and tabindex="-1" to fully suppress interaction.

Properties

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
size enum large Field height. large (44px) or small (36px). Applied via .search-field--small.
placeholder string Search Hint text shown when the field is empty. Disappears on focus.
state enum default Managed reactively. default at rest · active on focus (ink border, cursor) · typing once text is entered (delete button appears).

type string search Always use type="search" on the input to enable semantic search behaviour and OS-level gestures.

Accessibility

Attribute / PatternUsage
type="search"Tells browsers and screen readers this is a search input. Enables OS-level clear gesture on mobile.
aria-label="Search"Required on the input when no visible <label> is present.
aria-label="Clear search"Applied to the clear button so its purpose is announced.
role="search"Optional landmark on a wrapping <form> or <div> to aid navigation.
Keyboard: EscapeShould clear the field and/or dismiss the search overlay, returning focus to the trigger.
Focus managementWhen the search overlay opens, focus must move to the input immediately. On cancel, return focus to the triggering element.

Variants

State Unchecked Checked Indeterminate
Default
Hover

Accessibility

Built on a native input[type="checkbox"]. The browser handles checked/unchecked state announcements automatically. The indeterminate state must be set via JavaScript — it has no HTML attribute equivalent. Every checkbox must have an accessible name via a visible <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.

InteractionBehaviour
Tab / Shift+Tab Moves focus to and from the checkbox. Native <input> participates in the tab order automatically.
Space Toggles checked state when focused. Handled natively — no JavaScript needed.
aria-checked Set automatically by the browser from the checked and indeterminate properties. Indeterminate maps to aria-checked="mixed" — screen readers announce it as "mixed" or "partially checked".
indeterminate A JavaScript-only property (el.indeterminate = true). Visually shows a dash and is announced as "mixed" by screen readers. Commonly used for "select all" controls where only some children are checked.
aria-disabled Set automatically from the HTML disabled attribute. Disabled checkboxes remain in the reading order so screen reader users know the option exists.

Properties

Attribute Type Default Description
checked boolean false Sets the initial checked state.
indeterminate boolean (JS) false Shows a dash indicating partial selection. Set via el.indeterminate = true — no HTML attribute equivalent.
disabled boolean false Prevents interaction. Box renders in the disabled colour.
id string — Required when using a separate <label for="...">.

Accessibility

The switch is built on a native input[type="checkbox"] with role="switch". The browser automatically exposes the checked state to assistive technology. Every toggle must have an accessible name — either via a visible <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.

InteractionBehaviour
Tab / Shift+Tab Moves keyboard focus to and away from the toggle. Because this component uses a native <input>, it participates in the page tab order automatically — no extra implementation needed.
Space Flips the switch between on and off when focused. Again, native <input type="checkbox"> behaviour — the browser handles it for free.
role="switch" An ARIA attribute you add to the <input> element. It changes how screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA, TalkBack) announce the component. Without it, a screen reader says "checkbox, checked". With it, it says "switch, on" — which is semantically correct for a toggle. One attribute, meaningful difference for blind users.
aria-checked Tells screen readers whether the switch is currently on or off. You never write this yourself — the browser sets it automatically based on the checked state of the native input and keeps it in sync on every change.
aria-disabled Tells screen readers that this control exists but cannot be interacted with. The browser sets it automatically from the HTML disabled attribute. Crucially, disabled elements are not removed from the reading order — VoiceOver will still announce them, but describe them as "dimmed" or "unavailable", so the user knows the option exists but isn't available to them.
aria-label A plain-text string that gives the toggle an accessible name when there is no visible label in the UI. Screen readers read this string aloud when the user navigates to the toggle. Example: aria-label="Enable dark mode". If the toggle already has a visible <label> element associated via for, this attribute is not needed.

Properties

Attribute Type Default Description
checked boolean — Sets the initial checked (on) state. Omit for off.
disabled boolean false Prevents interaction. Track and icon render in the disabled colour.
id string — Required when the label is a separate element using for / aria-labelledby.
name string — Form field name submitted with the form.
value string "on" Form field value submitted when the switch is on.

Accessibility

Segmented Control is implemented as a tab widget — the track is a tablist and each segment is a tab.

Concern Implementation
Roles Track element receives role="tablist"; each tab receives role="tab".
Selection state The active tab carries aria-selected="true"; all others carry aria-selected="false".

Badges When a badge count is meaningful, annotate with an aria-label on the badge element (e.g. aria-label="9 unread") or include the count in the tab label via aria-label.

All configurable properties exposed on the Segmented Control component.

Property Type Default Notes

Accessibility

Stepper is a spinbutton widget — the input field carries the role and value attributes while the buttons are plain controls that manipulate it.

ConcernImplementation
Role The <input type="number"> natively receives role="spinbutton". Wrap the whole group in a <div role="group"> with aria-label describing what is being counted (e.g. aria-label="Quantity").
Value aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax are set automatically by type="number" with min / max attributes. Reflect the current value in the value attribute at all times.
Button labels Each button must have a descriptive aria-label — e.g. aria-label="Decrease quantity". Pair with aria-controls pointing to the input's id to declare the relationship.
Keyboard ↑ / ↓ arrows inside the field increment and decrement by the step value natively. Tab moves focus to the minus button, field, then plus button in order.
Disabled state Apply the disabled attribute to both buttons and the input when the stepper is inactive. Do not rely on pointer-events or opacity alone — disabled must be announced to assistive technology.
Min / max bounds Disable the decrement button when value equals min; disable the increment button when value equals max. Prevents silent out-of-range values from reaching form state.

Properties

All configurable properties exposed on the Stepper component.

PropertyTypeDefaultNotes
size enum small One of small · medium · large. Small: 32px buttons, 40px field, 18px text. Medium: 40px buttons, 48px field, 24px text. Large: 48px buttons, 56px field, 32px text.
value number 0 Current numeric value. Reflected in the input's value attribute.
min number 0 Lower bound. The decrement button is disabled when the value reaches this floor.
max number 999 Upper bound. The increment button is disabled when the value reaches this ceiling.
step number 1 Amount added or subtracted per button press. Also controls the arrow-key increment when the field has focus.
disabled boolean false When true, both buttons and the input are disabled and the entire stepper renders at 38% opacity.

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription

Accessibility

Attribute / PatternUsage
Back buttonUse <button aria-label="Go back">. Never use a generic icon without a label — "Go back" is the expected accessible name.
Icon buttonsEach <button> in the trailing area requires an aria-label describing its action (e.g., "Notifications", "Saved items").
Avatar buttonUse aria-label="Profile" or the user's name if personalised. The <img> inside should have alt="" (decorative) since the button label carries the accessible name.
Notification badgesBadges are decorative (aria-hidden="true"). Convey the unread count in the button's accessible name if precision matters: aria-label="Notifications, 3 unread".
Inline titleThe compact toolbar title is aria-hidden="true" — the page heading (<h1>) in the expandable area is the authoritative heading. Screen readers skip the duplicate.
Heading levelThe large heading uses <h1>. Ensure the page has only one <h1>; sub-sections use <h2> and below.
Keyboard: TabFocus moves through the back button (if present), then each icon button, then the avatar. The heading and inline title text are not focusable.

Icon only

Accessibility

Built on the ARIA tablist / tab pattern. The <nav> element provides a landmark so screen reader users can jump directly to the navigation. Only the active tab is in the tab order at any time (roving tabindex) — arrow keys move between tabs without leaving the component.

InteractionBehaviour
Tab / Shift+Tab Moves focus into and out of the tab bar. Only the currently active tab receives tab focus — inactive tabs have tabindex="-1" and are skipped.
← → Arrow keys Cycle focus and selection left or right through the tabs with wrapping. This is the standard tablist navigation pattern — users do not need to Tab through every option.
role="tablist" Applied to .bnav-track. Groups the tab buttons into a single navigable set and tells screen readers this is a tab bar, not a list of unrelated buttons.
role="tab" Applied to each .bnav-tab button. Screen readers announce the tab's accessible name (from aria-label) together with its selected state and position — e.g. "Home, tab, selected, 1 of 4".
aria-selected Set to "true" on the active tab and "false" on all others. Updated by initBnav on every selection change so the state is always in sync with the visual indicator.
aria-label on <nav> Names the navigation landmark. Without it VoiceOver announces "navigation" generically; with it, it announces the specific name (e.g. "Main navigation"). Required when a page has more than one <nav>.
aria-label on FAB The FAB has no visible text label, so aria-label is required to describe its action. Describe what it does, not what it looks like — e.g. aria-label="New post" not "Plus button".

Properties

ClassValuesDescription
bnav—Root <nav> element. Flex row containing the track and optional FAB.
bnav-track—Pill-shaped tab container on a div. Use position:relative — the animated pill is absolutely positioned inside.
bnav-pill—Sliding selection indicator on a span. Position and width are driven by initBnav on every tab change.
bnav-tab—Individual tab button. Always 40 × 40 px when unselected; expands to 96 px wide when bnav-tab--active is present.
bnav-tab--active—Modifier on bnav-tab. Expands the tab, fades in the label, and turns the icon to the inverse colour.
bnav-label—Tab label text in a span. Invisible (opacity 0) when unselected; fades in with a 60 ms delay when the tab becomes active.
bnav-fab—Floating action button — 56 × 56 px circle. Sits alongside the track. Requires an aria-label.
bnav--icon-only—Modifier on bnav. Hides all labels; the selected tab stays 40 × 40 px and the pill slides without expanding.
bnav--reversed—Modifier on bnav. For use on dark surfaces — inverts track and pill colours.

Accessibility

Tabs follow the ARIA tablist pattern. The strip is a tablist, each button is a tab, and each content region is a tabpanel. Only the active tab is reachable by Tab key — arrow keys navigate between tabs.

ConcernImplementation
Roles Tab strip receives role="tablist"; each tab receives role="tab"; each panel receives role="tabpanel".
Selection state Active tab carries aria-selected="true"; all others carry aria-selected="false". Do not remove inactive tabs from the DOM — use hidden on their panels instead.
Keyboard ← / → arrow keys move focus between tabs with wrapping. Home / End jump to first / last. Enter or Space activates the focused tab.
Tab / panel linkage Each tab carries aria-controls="panel-id" pointing to its panel; each panel carries aria-labelledby="tab-id" pointing back to its tab.
Tablist label Provide aria-label or aria-labelledby on the tablist to describe the set (e.g. aria-label="Product details").
Icons Leading and top icons are decorative. Always add aria-hidden="true" and ensure the text label provides the accessible name.

Properties

Configurable properties on the Tabs component.

PropertyTypeDefaultNotes
tabs 2 – 5 3 Number of tab items in the strip. Each tab hugs its label; tabs do not share equal width unless forced by a container grid.
leadingIcon boolean false Renders a 20×20 icon before the label on every tab. Mutually exclusive with topIcon. Mark the icon aria-hidden="true".
topIcon boolean false Renders a 20×20 icon above the label, stacking vertically. Mutually exclusive with leadingIcon. Increases tab height to 60px. Badge is not available in this configuration.
badge boolean | number false Shows a small numeric badge after the label (or after the leading icon). Not available when topIcon is true. Annotate with aria-label if the count is meaningful to screen readers.
selected number 0 Zero-based index of the initially selected tab. Controlled via aria-selected on each tab element.
disabled boolean false Per-tab property. Disabled tabs are skipped during arrow-key navigation and cannot be selected.

Each date item is a button with an accessible name including the full weekday and date — e.g. "Wednesday, 1". The strip uses role="tablist" so screen readers announce the component as a date selection group, and aria-selected tracks the active date.

InteractionBehaviour
Tab / Shift+Tab Moves focus into and out of the strip. Only the selected date button receives tab focus — all others use tabindex="-1".

dtab-strip-item—Wrapper button. Flex: 1 to fill the column. Contains a single dtab-strip-inner.
dtab-strip-inner—The 40 × 40 px circle shape. Default = transparent. Today = container fill + border. Selected = contrast fill.
dtab-item--selected—Active selection modifier. Fills the tab oval or strip circle with contrast colour and sets text to inverse. Always wins over dtab-item--today.
dtab-item--today—Marks today's date. Container fill + border in both Tab and Strip. Suppressed visually when dtab-item--selected is also present.
dtab-item--disabled—Non-interactive date. Reduces opacity to 35 % and removes pointer events.

PatternComponentGuidance
role="tablist" / role="tab"DotThe dot row is a tablist. Each dot is a tab with aria-selected and an aria-label like "Slide 2 of 4".
aria-label="Page navigation"PaginationWrap the numbered bar in a <nav> with a descriptive label to distinguish it from other navigation landmarks on the page.

KeyboardBothAll interactive elements must be reachable and operable via keyboard. Dots support arrow key navigation within the tablist; pagination buttons use standard focus order.

PropertyValuesNotes
TypeDot · PaginationDot for carousels, onboarding, and slideshows on mobile or desktop. Pagination for search results, tables, and data listings on the web.
Pages (Dot)2 · 3 · 4Keep dots to 4 or fewer. More than 4 lose their at-a-glance positional value. For longer sets consider a count label (2 / 7) instead.

Variants

The left accessory slot accepts five media types. Each carries semantic weight: success, attention, and danger map to system states; logo and avatar are used for brand or account context.

Logo

New update available

Version 2.4 is ready to install.

Avatar

Alex left a comment

Great work on the new layout!

Success

Changes saved

Your edits have been saved.

Attention

Heads up

This action may affect others.

Danger

Something went wrong

Please try again later.

Accessibility

Toasts surface information without interrupting focus. They use role="status" with aria-live="polite" so screen readers announce them at the next natural pause, and aria-atomic="true" ensures the full message is read when the content updates.

ConcernImplementation
Live region The toast container carries role="status", aria-live="polite", and aria-atomic="true". This ensures screen readers announce the full message at the next opportunity without interrupting the user mid-sentence.
Dismiss button The close button must have an accessible name: aria-label="Dismiss". It is always reachable by keyboard even when focus remains in the triggering context.
Media icons Left accessory icons (success, attention, danger, logo, avatar) are decorative. Mark them aria-hidden="true" — the semantic meaning must also be conveyed through the message text.
Auto-dismiss timing Toasts should persist for a minimum of 5 seconds before auto-dismissing, giving users with cognitive or motor difficulties enough time to read and react. Dismiss early if the user interacts with it.
Motion Entrance and exit animations should respect prefers-reduced-motion. When reduced motion is active, replace slide/fade transitions with a simple opacity change.
Focus management Do not move focus to the toast on appearance — this would disrupt the current user flow. Focus only moves to the toast if the user explicitly navigates to it via keyboard.

Properties

Configurable properties on the Toast component.

PropertyTypeDefaultNotes
leadingMedia logo · avatar · success · attention · danger success The media type shown in the left accessory slot. Semantic variants (success, attention, danger) communicate system state with colour. Logo and avatar provide brand or account context.
leftAccessory boolean true Shows or hides the left accessory slot. When hidden, the toast body text shifts to fill the full width.
title boolean true Toggles the title line. When both title and body are shown, the title is semibold and the body sits below at reduced opacity. When only one is shown, it renders in the title style.
body boolean true Toggles the body text line. Typically a brief description or follow-up to the title.
dismiss boolean true Shows or hides the dismiss (×) button. When hidden, the toast must auto-dismiss after a timeout — do not leave a toast with no way to remove it.
position top · bottom top Vertical anchor for the toast container. top pins it below the status bar with a slide-down entrance; bottom pins it above the home indicator with a slide-up entrance. Positioning is applied to the wrapping container, not the toast element itself.

Badge

A small visual indicator that communicates status or count. Dot badges signal unread activity without specifics; number badges display a quantity. Both come in info and alert types.

Preview

Icon · number

Variants

Size Dot · Info Dot · Alert Number · Info Number · Alert
Small 9 9
Large 9 9

Accessibility

Badges are purely visual — they carry no semantic meaning on their own. The surrounding interactive element (button, link, icon) must communicate the badge's meaning to screen readers via aria-label. Never rely on the badge alone to convey critical state.

PatternGuidance
Badge on a button Include the count in the button's aria-label: <button aria-label="Notifications, 5 unread">. The badge span should have aria-hidden="true".
Dot badge Always pair with a meaningful label on the parent: e.g. aria-label="Messages (new)". A dot alone gives no information.
Live updates If the count updates dynamically, wrap the badge in a role="status" or aria-live="polite" region so changes are announced.
Colour contrast Both info and alert backgrounds meet WCAG AA against white text at all supported sizes.

Properties

ClassValuesDescription
badge-dot — Base dot badge. A solid circle with a white separation ring.
badge-dot--{size} small · large 8px (small) or 12px (large) diameter.
badge-dot--alert — Switches fill to --color-danger. Default (info) uses --color-info.
badge-number — Base number badge. Pill-shaped container with semibold text.
badge-number--{size} small · large 18px height (small) or 24px height (large). Expands horizontally for multi-digit counts.
badge-number--alert — Switches fill to --color-danger. Default (info) uses --color-info.
badge-host — Wrapper for positioning a badge over another element. Set badge-host-badge on the badge itself.

Three ways to communicate loading state — a linear bar for page and section loading, a circular arc for contained loading zones, and the brand loader for full-screen splash contexts. The linear bar and circular arc are determinate, communicating progress toward a known endpoint. The brand loader is indeterminate — it signals activity during full-screen loading contexts where progress isn't measurable.

Accessibility

PatternComponentGuidance
role="progressbar"Linear · CircularApply to the track element. Screen readers announce this as a progress indicator; avoid wrapping a <div> without a role.
aria-valuenow / aria-valuemin / aria-valuemaxLinear · CircularRequired for determinate progress. aria-valuenow reflects the current value (0–100). Omit only if the end value is truly unknown.
aria-labelAllDescribe what is loading — e.g. aria-label="Uploading file". A generic "Loading" is acceptable when context makes the target obvious.
role="status"Brand LoaderUse role="status" on the brand loader rather than progressbar. It is a polite live region that announces when the loader appears without interrupting the user.
MotionAllWrap animations in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to disable or substitute a static state for users who have opted out of motion.

Properties

PropertyValuesNotes
TypeLinear · Circular · Brand LoaderLinear for page and section loading. Circular for contained zones (cards, dialogs). Brand Loader for full-screen splash screens only.
Value0 – 100Expressed as a percentage. Drive the linear fill via width: X%; the circular fill via stroke-dashoffset: 125.66 × (1 − X/100).
Size (Circular)48 × 48 pxFixed canvas. Stroke weight is always 4px. Do not resize the SVG viewBox — adjust display size via width and height attributes.
Size (Brand Loader)64 px expanded · 48 px contractedThe pulse animation cycles between these two sizes via CSS scale. Never render it smaller than 48px at rest.
Track colorcolor-border-subtleThe inactive track background. Resolves to the same subtle gray in both light and dark modes.
Fill colorcolor-background-contrastNear-black in light mode; cream/white in dark mode. Maintains high contrast against the track in both themes automatically.

Components · Overlays

Scrim

A full-surface overlay layer that sits between the page and elevated content like modals, drawers, and bottom sheets. It dims and blurs the background, signals that the UI below is temporarily inaccessible, and provides a tap target for dismissal.

Stable v1.0 Web · Mobile Figma ↗

Preview

  • Mobile
  • Tablet
  • Desktop

HTML

<!-- Overlay container — must be position: relative, fixed, or absolute -->
<div class="overlay-container">

  <!-- Page content — apply inert when overlay is open -->
  <main inert><!-- page content --></main>

  <!-- Scrim — sibling of the elevated surface, behind it via z-index -->
  <div class="scrim-layer" aria-hidden="true"></div>

  <!-- Elevated surface (modal, sheet, drawer) sits above -->
  <div role="dialog" aria-modal="true">
    <!-- dialog content -->
  </div>

</div>

CSS

.scrim-layer {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  z-index: 1;
  background: rgba(8, 5, 13, 0.50);      /* light mode — ink at 50% */
  backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
  pointer-events: none;                   /* set to auto if scrim is tap-dismissible */
  transition: opacity 300ms ease;
}

[data-theme="dark"] .scrim-layer {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.50);  /* dark mode — white at 50% */
}

/* Optional: tap-dismissible scrim */
.scrim-layer[role="button"] {
  pointer-events: auto;
  cursor: pointer;
}

Tokens

The scrim is defined by two fill values — one per color mode — and a single blur. There are no size variants; it always fills its positioned container.

Property Mode Value Notes
background Light rgba(8, 5, 13, 0.50) Ink at 50% opacity. Darkens the background without fully obscuring it.
background Dark rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.50) White at 50% opacity. Same perceptual weight on dark backgrounds.
backdrop-filter Both blur(48px) Figma spec. CSS backdrop-filter produces equivalent visual output at a lower radius (~12px) due to renderer differences — adjust to match the intended look in your implementation.
transition Both opacity 300ms ease Fade in on open, fade out on close. No transform — just opacity.
z-index Both 1 Above page content, below the elevated surface (modal, sheet, drawer). Adjust to your stacking context.

Accessibility

The scrim is a structural affordance, not a content element. Its accessibility role is to block and redirect interaction — not to convey information.

Pattern Guidance
aria-hidden Mark the scrim element with aria-hidden="true". It has no semantic meaning — screen readers should traverse directly to the elevated content above it.
inert Apply the inert attribute to all page content behind the scrim when an overlay is open. This prevents focus, click, and screen-reader traversal in the background without needing aria-hidden on every sibling.
Dismissal If the scrim is tap-dismissible, also handle Escape on keyboard. The scrim can be a <button> or use role="button" with a keydown listener. Always ensure a visible close affordance exists within the overlay content itself.
Focus trap When the overlay above the scrim is open, trap focus within it. Focus must not reach elements behind the scrim. Return focus to the trigger element on dismissal.
Motion The scrim's opacity fade is subtle and low-risk on its own. When paired with overlay entrance animations, honor prefers-reduced-motion for the overlay's transform — the scrim opacity can remain.

Usage

Context Guidance
Modal dialogs Always pair a modal with a scrim. It communicates that the rest of the UI is temporarily blocked and provides a touch target for light-dismiss.
Bottom sheets Use a scrim with modal bottom sheets. Non-modal sheets — persistent, peek, or inline — do not need one.
Drawers Navigation and context drawers that overlap page content use a scrim. Inline drawers that push content do not.
Image lightboxes Use a scrim when a lightbox or full-screen media viewer replaces the page context. The blur softens the background without a hard-cut to black.
Stacking Never stack two scrims. If a second overlay opens above the first, keep a single scrim and raise only the topmost surface's z-index.

GuidelineNotes
Use sparinglyModals are highly interruptive. Reserve them for critical decisions, destructive actions, or focused tasks that cannot be completed inline.

Accessibility

Bottom sheets use the dialog role with aria-modal="true" to create a modal context. Focus should be trapped inside the sheet while open and returned to the trigger element on close.

Attribute / PatternUsage
role="dialog" Applied to the sheet container. Tells screen readers this is a dialog and pauses interaction with the background content.
aria-modal="true" Signals that content behind the sheet is inert. Prevents screen readers from navigating outside the sheet while it is open.
aria-label / aria-labelledby Names the dialog. Use aria-label when the sheet has no visible heading; use aria-labelledby pointing at .bs-title when a heading is present.
Focus management Move focus into the sheet on open (first focusable element or the dialog container). Loop focus within the sheet. On close, restore focus to the trigger element.
Escape key Always closes the sheet and returns focus to the trigger. This is the standard dialog dismissal pattern expected on all platforms.
Scrim / backdrop Make the scrim keyboard-accessible via Escape or a visible "Close" button. The scrim itself can be a button element or handle click with a complementary keyboard listener.
inert Apply inert to all page content behind the scrim when the sheet is open. Prevents background focus and screen reader traversal without needing aria-hidden on every sibling.

Properties

ClassValuesDescription
bottom-sheet — Root container. Anchors to the bottom edge of its positioned parent. Applies top corner radius, padding, vertical gap, and elevation shadow.
bottom-sheet--reversed — Dark-surface variant. Switches background to color-background-contrast and inverts all text, button, and media accent tokens.
bottom-sheet--card — Standalone display modifier. Rounds all four corners for use in documentation, onboarding previews, or any context where the sheet is not anchored to a screen edge.
bs-grabber — 44 × 4 px pill handle, centered at the top of the sheet. Uses primitive-ink-300 — same in both modes, as it sits against the sheet background rather than the scrim.
bs-media-logo — 48 px circular logo badge. Background is color-background-contrast (dark) in standard mode and color-inverse (white) in reversed mode — maintaining contrast for the enclosed brand mark.
bs-media-icon-bullet — 48 px circular icon container. Background: primitive-violet-300 (standard) · primitive-pool-300 (reversed). Both are light-value colours — icon always uses primitive-ink-900.
bs-media-avatar — 48 px circular avatar <img>. Apply object-fit: cover to preserve proportions regardless of source dimensions.
bs-title — Heading text. Serif typeface, bold, font-size-heading-l (32 px / 40 lh). Inverts to color-inverse in reversed mode.
bs-body — Supporting body copy. Sans-serif, font-size-body-m, regular weight. Inverts to color-inverse in reversed mode.
bs-actions — Horizontal button group container. 80 px min-height, flex row, 16 px gap. Each child bs-btn takes equal width via flex: 1.
bs-btn-filled — Primary action. Background color-action-default; reversed: color-action-inverse-default (white) with dark label.
bs-btn-outlined — Secondary action. Border color-border-strong, label color-content-default; reversed: color-border-inverse with color-inverse label.

Accessibility

ConcernImplementation
Container role Wrap the calendar in role="dialog" with aria-modal="true" and aria-label="Choose date" when presented as an overlay.
Grid semantics The day grid uses role="grid". Each row is role="row" and each cell is role="gridcell". Day buttons carry aria-label="Day, Month Date" (e.g. Thursday, May 14) and aria-pressed="true/false" for selection state.
Keyboard navigation Arrow keys move focus between days. Enter / Space select a date. Page Up / Page Down navigate months. Home / End jump to the first and last day of the current week. Escape closes the overlay.
Range selection Announce start date with aria-live="polite": "Start date selected: May 14. Select an end date." On completion: "Date range selected: May 14 to May 20."
Month navigation Prev/next buttons carry aria-label="Previous month" / "Next month". The month heading is marked with aria-live="polite" so changes are announced.
Disabled dates Unavailable cells use aria-disabled="true" and tabindex="-1". Do not use the native disabled attribute as it removes the element from the accessibility tree.
Focus management On open, focus is placed on today's date or the current selection. On close, focus returns to the trigger element that opened the picker.
Colour contrast Citron at -300 and all other accent colours at -200 achieve ≥ 4.5 : 1 contrast against primitive-ink-900 label text on the reversed surface. The standard dark circle (color-background-contrast) achieves ≥ 7 : 1.

Properties

Class / propertyValuesDescription
.dp—Calendar root. Sets the --dp-accent custom property to primitive-citron-300 by default.
.dp--reversed—Reversed surface variant. Switches all internal tokens to their -inverse counterparts and uses --dp-accent for the selected circle.
--dp-accentCSS custom propertyAccent colour for the selected state on the reversed surface. Citron uses -300; all other colour families use -200 for softer contrast on the dark surface. Only active when .dp--reversed is present.
.dp-day—Individual date cell. Interactive; fires click and keydown events.
.dp-day--today—Marks the current date. Renders a color-brand-cream fill with a color-border-default inset ring.
.dp-day--selected—Applied to range start and end endpoints. Renders a filled circle using color-background-contrast (standard) or --dp-accent (reversed).
.dp-day--range—Applied to days between the start and end of a range. Renders a full-width color-background-ui band (standard) or color-background-inverse-selection (reversed).
.dp-day--range-start—Range start endpoint. Combines .dp-day--selected with a right-half range band extending to adjacent in-range days.
.dp-day--range-end—Range end endpoint. Combines .dp-day--selected with a left-half range band.
.dp-day--disabled—Unavailable date. Uses color-content-disabled (standard) or color-content-inverse-disabled (reversed). Non-interactive.
.dp-day--other-month—Overflow days from the previous or next month. Rendered at reduced opacity, non-interactive.
.dp-compact-sheet—Bottom-sheet panel for the compact variant. Pair with .dp-compact-sheet--reversed to apply the contrast background.

Accessibility

Cards are non-interactive containers by default. All interactive elements inside — buttons, toggles, links — carry their own ARIA roles. Decorative photos and icons use aria-hidden="true".

Keyboard interaction

KeyAction
TabMove focus to the next interactive element inside the card (buttons, links).
Shift + TabMove focus to the previous interactive element.
Enter / SpaceActivate the focused button or link inside the card.

Roles & semantics

ElementGuidance
articleUse <article> when the card represents a self-contained piece of content (e.g. a blog post card). Use a plain <div> for UI panels.
img[alt]Always provide meaningful alt text for content photos. Use alt="" for purely decorative images alongside visible text.
button[aria-label]Icon-only buttons (back, favourite) must have a descriptive aria-label. Avoid redundant labels that duplicate adjacent visible text.
aria-pressedThe favourite button uses aria-pressed to communicate toggle state. Update this attribute whenever the visual state changes.
role="separator"The .divider element in the Multifunctional card footer carries role="separator" to communicate the visual break to screen readers.

Properties

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
type enum navigation Cell interaction model. navigation — the entire row is a tap target that navigates to a new screen. action — the row hosts an inline control (radio, checkbox, switch, or stepper); only the control itself is interactive.
leading enum none Leading media slot. One of none · icon · icon-bullet · avatar.
trailing enum caret Trailing slot. Navigation cells use caret by default. Action cells accept radio · checkbox · switch · stepper.
label string — Primary row text. Required.
overline boolean false Short all-caps label rendered above the primary text. Use for category or section context.
caption boolean true Supporting text rendered below the label. Accepts a secondary line of detail.
divider boolean true Horizontal rule separating cells. Omit on the last row of a group or when the list sits on a sectioned background.

Accessibility

Attribute / PatternUsage
Navigation cellWrap the entire row in a <button> or <a>. The row tap target must be at least 44×44 pt. Include an aria-label if the label text alone is ambiguous.
Action cellOnly the trailing control (<input>, <button>) should be interactive. The surrounding row is presentational. Associate the control with its label via aria-labelledby pointing at the .list-cell__label element.
role="list" / role="listitem"Apply role="list" to the wrapping container and role="listitem" to each cell when the list conveys a meaningful group relationship.
Keyboard: TabNavigation cells and action controls must be reachable by tab. Non-interactive row content should not receive focus.
Keyboard: Enter / SpaceActivates the focused navigation cell or control.
State announcementSwitch, checkbox, and radio controls announce their checked/unchecked state natively via their <input> type. No additional ARIA is needed.

<div class="list-accordion">

          aria-expanded="false"

    <div class="list-accordion__content">

      </div>
      <!-- Accordion control: only this element shows hover/pressed -->
      <div class="list-accordion__control">
        <div class="list-accordion__control-inner">
          <svg class="list-accordion__chevron"
               width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24"
               fill="currentColor" aria-hidden="true">
            <use href="#ico-caret-dn"/>

        </div>
      </div>

  </button>
  <div class="list-accordion__body" id="body-id" role="region">
    <div class="list-accordion__body-inner">

    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="list-accordion__divider"></div>
</div>

Variants & States

Hover and pressed states are isolated to the 40×40 chevron control — the label row carries no visual state layer. The chevron persists in its hover style while the panel is open.

Default

Open

Receive push notifications for real-time updates, or switch to a daily email digest. You can enable both.

Properties

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
label string — Primary header text. Required.
body string | slot — Content revealed when expanded. Accepts a text string for simple FAQs or a custom content slot for richer layouts.
open boolean false Controls the expanded state. Set to true to open on render. Reflected on the header's aria-expanded attribute.
leading boolean false Shows a leading icon slot in the header row. Use to visually reinforce the topic category.
overline boolean false Short all-caps label rendered above the primary header text.
caption boolean false Supporting text rendered below the label in the header row.
divider boolean true Horizontal rule below the accordion row. Omit on the last item in a group.
disabled boolean false Prevents the header from being toggled. The chevron control dims and pointer events are removed.

Accessibility

The accordion header is a <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing to the body panel's id. The body panel carries role="region" for landmark navigation.

Attribute / PatternUsage
aria-expanded="false|true"Set on the header button. Reflects the open/closed state of the body panel.
aria-controls="[body-id]"Links the header button to its body panel by ID.
role="region"Applied to the body panel so screen readers can navigate to it as a landmark.
Keyboard: Enter / SpaceToggles the accordion (native button behavior).
Keyboard: TabMoves focus between accordion headers. Body content is not focusable when collapsed.
Reduced motionRespect prefers-reduced-motion — skip or shorten the height animation.

Accessibility

Avatars are purely presentational. The <img> element should have a descriptive alt attribute when the user's identity is meaningful in context (e.g. "Sofia Esposito's avatar"), or an empty alt="" when the avatar is decorative and the user's name appears nearby. The initials variant is wrapped in a span with aria-hidden="true" — the surrounding element should carry the accessible name.

PatternGuidance
Photo with nearby name Use alt="" — the name in the UI provides the accessible label.
Photo without nearby name Use alt="[Name]'s avatar" so screen readers can identify the person.
Initials fallback Hide the initials with aria-hidden="true" and provide the full name via aria-label on the parent container.
Clickable avatar Wrap in an <a> or <button> and provide a label that describes the action, e.g. "View Sofia's profile".

Properties

Class Values Description
avatar--{size} xsmall · small · medium · large · xlarge · xxlarge Sets the avatar dimensions: 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 56 / 64 px.
avatar--{shape} circle · squircle · diamond · cushion Applies the clip-path for each shape variant.
avatar-img — Photo variant. Uses object-fit: cover — works with any aspect ratio.
avatar-initials — Initials fallback. Renders semibold text on a café-200 background, sized relative to the avatar.

Divider

A horizontal rule for separating content regions. Three stroke weights let you tune visual weight — from a hairline separator between list items to a bold accent block between major sections.

Stable v1.0 Web Mobile Figma ↗

Preview

The divider fills the width of its container by default. Apply a fixed width inline when a specific measure is required.

Thin

Medium

Thick

<!-- Thin — between list items or inline content -->
<hr class="divider divider--thin" aria-hidden="true">

<!-- Medium — between subsections -->
<hr class="divider divider--medium" aria-hidden="true">

<!-- Thick — major section break or accent -->
<hr class="divider divider--thick" aria-hidden="true">

<!-- Fixed width -->
<hr class="divider divider--thin" style="width: 240px;" aria-hidden="true">

Variants

Variant Height Token Example
Thin 1px color-border-default
Medium 4px color-border-subtle
Thick 8px color-border-subtle

Accessibility

Dividers are almost always decorative. Use aria-hidden="true" on the <hr> element to remove it from the accessibility tree — screen readers communicate section structure through headings and landmarks, not visual rules.

Usage patterns

PatternGuidance
Decorative (most cases) Add aria-hidden="true". The divider is a visual aid; heading hierarchy and landmark regions convey document structure to assistive technology.
Semantic separator If the divider genuinely separates two distinct content regions with no heading present, omit aria-hidden. The native <hr> element carries an implicit role="separator".
Non-semantic element If you use a <div> instead of <hr>, add role="separator" explicitly — or aria-hidden="true" if decorative.

Properties

ClassDescription
divider Base class. Sets width: 100%, removes default <hr> border. Apply a weight modifier below.
divider--thin 1px height. Uses color-border-default. For separating items within a list or between tightly related content.
divider--medium 4px height, rounded ends. Uses color-border-subtle. For subsection breaks or grouped content.
divider--thick 8px height, rounded ends. Uses color-border-subtle. For major section breaks or tonal accent blocks.

Accessibility

Icon Bullet is a purely decorative element and carries no interactive meaning. It should always be hidden from assistive technology so screen readers skip it entirely. If the icon communicates meaning that is not expressed in adjacent text, add a visually-hidden label using aria-label on a wrapping element instead.

InteractionBehaviour
aria-hidden="true" Always applied to .icon-bullet. Removes the element from the accessibility tree so screen readers skip it.
focusable Never. Icon Bullet is non-interactive and should not receive keyboard focus. Do not place it inside a <button> or <a> unless the entire interactive element has its own accessible label.
role None required. The element is presentational. Screen readers receive no role, name, or state for this element when aria-hidden is set.
Contextual meaning If color alone conveys meaning (e.g. red = danger), ensure the surrounding text or an aria-label on a parent communicates the same information.

Properties

ClassValuesDescription
icon-bullet — Base class. Apply to a <span>. Always combine with one size and one color modifier.
icon-bullet--xlarge 56px Largest size. 12px padding, 32px icon area. Default for Bottom Sheet and feature-callout layouts.
icon-bullet--large 48px Standard large size. 12px padding, 24px icon area.
icon-bullet--medium 40px Medium size. 10px padding, 20px icon area. Suited to dense lists.
icon-bullet--small 32px Smallest size. 8px padding, 16px icon area. Use in compact contexts.
icon-bullet--white color-inverse White circle with dark icon. Designed for placement on dark or colored surfaces.
icon-bullet--ink color-background-contrast Ink-dark circle with white icon. Highest contrast; adapts to dark mode.
icon-bullet--violet violet-300 Lavender circle — the ůnica brand accent color.
icon-bullet--berry berry-300 Pink-rose circle.
icon-bullet--apricot apricot-300 Warm peach circle.
icon-bullet--mint mint-300 Cool green circle.
icon-bullet--pool pool-300 Bright teal circle.
icon-bullet--citron citron-300 Yellow-green circle.
